items.note: 12-week classroom experiment with 120 animation students in GAI-supported versus conventional teaching; outcomes are pre/post learning tests and surveys, and the abstract claims creative expression without a clear rated creativity score on student output.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page all failed); per search notes, freshmen in an experimental group saw text-to-video clips during pre-writing brainstorming versus a control group, and idea counts and time were assessed; N and allocation unknown.

Natural experiment on GitHub Copilot's launch (Python supported, R not) showing contributions rose 28 to 40 percent, more in incremental than substantive (new-functionality) work; real-world output with a novelty-type outcome, no assigned creative task; SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.4684662 is the same study.

System paper (AToM CoWriter, proactive writing support inferred from cognitive processes) with two within-subjects studies (N = 21) reporting better expressiveness and idea exploration; unclear whether these are rated on the writing or self-reported, and the comparison condition is not described; well under 50 participants.

System paper (Surprise2Refine, axis-centered agent-assisted design tool) with a within-subjects study of 14 designers reporting higher sense of control and perceived creativity of design outcomes; perceived creativity may be self-rated, so it may fall to self_report_only; well under 50 participants.

12-week quasi-experiment with 118 design students: a value-sensitive custom text-to-image pipeline (LoRA, ControlNet) versus traditional methods; outcomes are aesthetic appreciation, design implementation, and cultural identity, so a creativity score on output is not stated.

Quasi-experimental data relating dimensions of human-AI interaction (cognitive, informative, logical) and skill level to novelty and usefulness of creative outputs; reads as a correlational analysis within AI users, and whether a no-AI or alternative-AI arm exists is not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect blocked); title suggests AI compositional tools in choral education and students' arrangement creativity, but design, comparison, and N are unknown.

Pre/post quasi-experiment with 85 digital media students in intact classes assigned to GAI-assisted versus traditional advertising design instruction; design performance including creativity scored, ANCOVA on post-test; non-random assignment, so likely observational in the core sense.

Mixed-method experiment with 160 novice designers across four AI-support conditions (unstructured versus scaffolded text-to-image use, among others); expert-judged quality and originality plus similarity metrics for visual diversity; assignment method not stated in the abstract.
